conventionally

/kuhn-VEN-shuh-nuh-lee/ - the stress falls on VEN · adverb

Hear It

What It Means

Conventionally means in the customary or widely accepted way.

Traders in the pit still conventionally seal a deal with a handshake, even now that the paperwork is electronic.

Example

Ahead of every concert the oboist sounds a single A, and the whole orchestra tunes to it. Nothing in physics elevates the oboe; several instruments hold pitch as well or better. But ensembles conventionally tune this way, and have for two hundred years — so when a youth orchestra in Reykjavik began tuning to a struck bell instead, visiting conductors needed a moment to recover.

Conventionally is the exact word because it describes what is done in the customary or widely accepted way — the path worn smooth by general agreement, not by rule or law. No rule crowns the oboe; agreement does. The word carries a quiet second message: this is how it is usually done, so eyebrows go up when someone does otherwise.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

customarily: Customarily describes the settled practice of one particular place or group — what this village, this court, this firm always does. Conventionally is wider: the way most people everywhere have accepted as proper. A custom belongs to somebody in particular; a convention belongs to everybody.

traditionally: Traditionally means in the way handed down from earlier generations — a practice kept because forebears kept it, whatever the present thinks of it. Conventionally makes no claim about age or origin: it says only that people today accept this as the standard way. Tradition looks backward; convention looks around.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

unusually: departing from the common run

rebelliously: in open defiance of the accepted way

Where it sits · how binding the shared way has become

typically → conventionally → ritually

typically vs. conventionally: Typically only reports what usually happens; conventionally adds that people have accepted it as the proper way.

ritually vs. conventionally: Ritually goes past conventionally — the practice has hardened into a fixed rite, performed the same way every time as if the steps themselves were sacred.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-: together

Root — ven: to come (Latin venire)

Suffix — -tion: act or result of

Suffix — -al: relating to

Suffix — -ly: in the manner of

Put it together: Con- (together) + ven (to come) + -tion + -al + -ly = in the manner of a coming-together. A convention is literally what people have 'come together' on — an agreement nobody signed but everybody keeps. Do a thing conventionally and you do it the way the group long ago settled on doing it.

Use the root in a new word: venue: The concert's venue is simply the place everyone comes to for the event.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral

Conventionally describes doing things the widely accepted way, with no claim about age or origin — its cousin traditionally reaches back through generations instead. And when a practice has dug in so hard that reformers bounce off it, this unit's entrenched is the word waiting: a convention becomes entrenched at the moment attempts to change it start failing.
